evidence.text: Numerically solve the background Klein–Gordon and Hubble equations as a first-order system using Y1=φ/Mp, Y2=φ̇/(Mp H0), and ln(a) as the independent variable. Perturbation equations are presented in conformal Newtonian and synchronous gauges.

sources.title: Constraint on the equation of state parameter ($\omega$) in non-minimally coupled $f(Q)$ gravity

evidence.text: Bayesian MCMC estimates marginal posterior distributions for α, n and ω using a likelihood proportional to exp(−χ²/2). Reported parameter errors are 1σ, or 68%; contour plots are described as showing 68% and 95% confidence regions.

sources.title: Constraints on quintessence scalar field models using cosmological observations

evidence.text: CosmoMC samples seven parameters: six standard cosmological parameters plus μ=β, α or δ. The authors require Gelman–Rubin R−1<0.1 and report continuing every chain until approximately R−1≤0.03; marginalized intervals and contours are reported at 68% and 95% CL.

sources.title: Constraints on quintessence scalar field models using cosmological observations

evidence.text: Use Om(z)=[E(z)^2−1]/[(1+z)^3−1], E=H/H0, as a background diagnostic. Bayesian evidence integrates likelihood times prior and is estimated from the MCMC chains with MCEvidence. Bij is evidence for the scalar model divided by evidence for ΛCDM; negative ln Bij favors ΛCDM.

sources.title: Constraint on the equation of state parameter ($\omega$) in non-minimally coupled $f(Q)$ gravity

evidence.text: The Hubble likelihood uses a sum of squared Hth−Hobs residuals divided by observational variances. The supernova likelihood uses distance-modulus residuals and the Pantheon covariance matrix, with DL=(1+z)c∫0^z dẑ/H(ẑ) and μth=5log10[DL/(10 pc)].

sources.title: Constraint on the equation of state parameter ($\omega$) in non-minimally coupled $f(Q)$ gravity

evidence.text: Metric variation yields modified Friedmann equations involving F=f1′+2f2′LM. The authors integrate the selected continuity equation and insert their functions f1 and f2 to obtain the model H(z) used in observational fitting.

destination.title: Thermal and transient acceleration
destination.question: How can hidden-sector interactions or particle production sustain acceleration and alter its duration, signatures or possible endpoint?
destination.summary: Provide related but distinct homes for thermal hidden-sector acceleration, interaction-supported transient dark energy and radiation-producing rolling fields.

systems: Scalars interacting with hidden matter, radiation or subdominant quintessence
targets: Duration of acceleration and possible turnaround
regimes: Finite-temperature evolution without ordinary slow roll
Positive-to-negative potential evolution in a specified branch
assumptions: Absence of a zero-temperature de Sitter vacuum and absence of ordinary slow roll are source-specific restrictions.
Temperature-independent and temperature-dependent production mechanisms are alternatives.
conventions: Produced thermal radiation and an initially internally thermalised hidden sector are distinct setups.
includes: Alternate mechanisms outside a narrow slowly rolling canonical core
excludes: A demonstrated bounce or complete contraction history

readingCoverage.readingLimit: The thermal hidden-sector and transient-mechanism targets have description support. The radiating-field excerpt is explicitly v2 dated 19 May 2026 and primarily follows the turnaround branch through its expansion phase.

sources.title: Thermal Dark Energy

evidence.text: Thermal and quantum vacuum-decay actions are computed numerically by an overshoot/undershoot method using modified CosmoTransitions code. The thin-wall approximation is stated to be extremely inaccurate for these configurations.

sources.title: Dark energy with the help of interacting dark sectors

evidence.text: Coupled scalar and Friedmann equations are solved numerically with visible radiation and additional dominant dark matter. A preliminary relativistic linear perturbation analysis uses synchronous gauge.

sources.title: Particle production by time-varying dark energy and the end of cosmic expansion

evidence.text: Compare constant and temperature-dependent dissipation across both potentials. For VII, the numerical discussion stops expansion at H=0 and switches the Hubble sign for contraction. Analytic growth-rate comparisons and an effective radiation equation of state supplement the contracting numerical examples.

sources.title: Thermal Dark Energy

evidence.text: The authors use a one-loop thermal effective potential summed over thermalised species, employing full thermal functions for plots and high/low-temperature expansions for interpretation. They report that daisy resummation does not significantly change their models' allowed parameter space.

sources.title: Dark energy with the help of interacting dark sectors

evidence.text: Thermal analysis uses a one-loop high-temperature effective potential and Lambert W minima. Quantum and thermal escape rates are estimated with approximate no-barrier potentials and O(4)/O(3) Euclidean bounces.

sources.title: Dark energy with the help of interacting dark sectors

evidence.text: Time averaging coherent ψ oscillations gives an approximate trapping potential. Rescaling ϕ yields a Mathieu equation; Floquet exponents and their competition with Hubble damping constrain parametric resonance, including nonzero momentum modes.

destination.title: Perturbations, growth and clustering
destination.question: Which linear perturbation, matter-power and CMB–galaxy observables can distinguish the supplied dark-energy mechanisms?
destination.summary: Separate calculations of model perturbations from forecasts for measuring the scale and amplitude of dark-energy clustering.

targets: Scale and amplitude of dark-energy clustering
assumptions: The canonical scalar is a tested model or comparison, not a shared kinetic action for every entry.
ISW forecasts retain their source survey and initial-condition assumptions.
conventions: A forecasted correlation measurement is not an observed detection of dark-energy clustering.
includes: Slotheon comparisons with canonical quintessence and ΛCDM
excludes: Inferring a background-model equivalence from similar perturbation curves

sources.title: Measuring dark energy clustering with CMB-galaxy correlations

evidence.text: How well can future CMB–galaxy correlations constrain the physical scale and amplitude of dark-energy clustering, and thereby test canonical single-scalar quintessence?

sources.title: Dark Energy, the Swampland and the Equivalence Principle

evidence.text: Can early suppression of a scalar-mediated dark-matter force permit appreciable attraction today while retaining acceptable expansion and structure formation? The paper also asks whether the interaction can slow quintessence sufficiently to accommodate a larger exponential-potential slope.

sources.title: No $H_0$ assistance from assisted quintessence

evidence.text: Can an assisted-quintessence scaling field connect early and late dark energy while raising the CMB-inferred Hubble constant into agreement with the historical SH0ES determination, once linear perturbations are included?

sources.title: Evolution of Dark Energy Perturbations for Slotheon Field and Power Spectrum

evidence.text: How do background evolution, linear dark-energy and matter perturbations, and the matter power spectrum behave for thawing Slotheon dark energy, relative to the paper's canonical-quintessence and ΛCDM calculations?

sources.title: Cosmology With Axionic-quintessence Coupled with Dark Matter

evidence.text: Can phenomenological coupling of PST axionic quintessence to dark matter permit larger departures from cosmological-constant behavior while satisfying the paper's background-expansion and linear-growth data?

sources.title: Super-acceleration as signature of dark sector interaction

evidence.text: Can interaction between canonical quintessence and dark matter generate an inferred dark-energy equation of state below −1 when observations are analyzed assuming noninteracting CDM, and what distance, matter-density and structure-growth signatures could reveal the interaction?
